evidence.detail: KeyframeAnimation decodes one rs/u/c value per curve record, uses rs/u/c.b() as the channel-array width, and routes the record either to the skeletal/bone transform matrix or the legacy Skeleton transform array according to this value.

The six instances expose dimensions 0, 9, 3, 6, 1 and 3; the nine-channel instance is exactly the rotation/translation/scale bone transform family and the one-channel instance marks transparency/alpha modification.

A public client implementation containing the same "Not a keyframe file!" format has an exact six-instance matching class named AnimTransform with NULL, VERTEX, COLOUR and TRANSPARENCY roles and the same dimension counts.

candidates.note: AnimationTransformType is a conservative semantic recovery name for the exact v308 role; public deobfuscated client code is corroborating evidence only, while exact v308 bytecode remains authoritative.

evidence.detail: KeyframeAnimation decodes one rs/u/e value per curve and uses rs/u/e.c() solely as the component index into the selected transform-type channel array.
The type has 17 encoded instances whose component values include rotation indices 0-2, translation 3-5, scale 6-8, transparency 0 and additional non-bone property channels.

The same keyframe format in a public client source exposes the exact 17-instance table as AnimationChannel with ROTATE_X/Y/Z, TRANSLATE_X/Y/Z, SCALE_X/Y/Z, TRANSPARENCY and additional property channels.

candidates.note: AnimationChannel is a conservative semantic recovery name for the exact v308 role; public deobfuscated client code is corroborating evidence only, while exact v308 bytecode remains authoritative.

evidence.detail: rs/u/f contains no instance state or behavior; it defines exactly Math.ulp(1.0F) and twice that value.
AnimationCurve uses those two values as epsilon/threshold constants throughout cubic control-point clamping and polynomial root/interpolation comparisons.
The matching public keyframe implementation exposes the same two float values in a constants-only helper used by curve interpolation.

candidates.note: InterpolationConstants is a conservative semantic recovery name for the exact v308 role; public deobfuscated client code is corroborating evidence only, while exact v308 bytecode remains authoritative.

evidence.detail: rs/u/h stores a float[] coefficient vector and an integer degree/count, evaluates that vector with Horner's method, and can derive the coefficient vector for the polynomial derivative.
AnimationCurve constructs rs/u/h while recursively solving interpolation polynomials and passes it into the bracketed root/bisection routine.
The matching public keyframe implementation exposes the same coefficient/count wrapper as InterpolationChain and uses it only in the interpolation polynomial root solver.

candidates.note: InterpolationPolynomial is a conservative semantic recovery name for the exact v308 role; public deobfuscated client code is corroborating evidence only, while exact v308 bytecode remains authoritative.
